payload.brief:
USER QUESTION: How do citations flow between research fields within Columbia's own papers (Columbia papers citing other Columbia papers)? Show the flows as a Sankey diagram.
GOAL: Join the citations with citing and cited snapshot works, classify fields and deliver complete field-pair counts plus a compact findings artifact for this straightforward aggregate. 
INPUTS: none
DEFINITIONS: Internal citations are distinct directed citing-work → cited-work pairs with both endpoints in the Columbia-affiliated 2021–2024 snapshot (all work types); assign each work one OpenAlex field via its primary topic, falling back to highest-scored assigned topic only when primary-topic information is unavailable, with stable tie-breaking. Keep unclassified as a separate bucket; count same-field pairs and identify cross-field pairs separately. Unclassified endpoint pairs are excluded from denominator for calculating same vs cross among classified, but report all counts. Check for any self-loop anomalies and report handling; don't erase coauthor self-citations.
ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA: Reconcile pair totals with both-classified and unclassified and both-classified same-field plus cross-field. Provide field ids, names and counts with directional endpoints, and optionally domain. Provide key stats including strongest same- and cross-field links and coverage. For the Sankey provide total and number of links under reasonable default filters (e.g. top 25 links with all vs cross only) if possible. Ensure artifacts have recorded definitions. 
OUTPUT: Save and report artifact ids, schemas, numerical findings and caveats.

payload.decision: Use all 2021–2024 snapshot works regardless of type; require both citation endpoints to join to works, and deduplicate ordered work-ID pairs. Drop identical work-ID self-loops as anomalies if present (none observed); do not filter shared-author citations. Classify by the field mapped from works.primary_topic_id, otherwise use a mapped assigned topic (flagged primary first if available, then highest score, lower rank, ascending topic ID). Use UNCLASSIFIED as a separate field ID for remaining works. Same/cross are defined only for pairs with two classified endpoints; unclassified endpoint pairs remain in overall totals.

The complete field-pair table contains every observed positive-count ordered bucket pair; absent pairs have zero count. Sankey nodes are separate by endpoint role (citing left, cited right), including same-field flows. Independently rank all observed links and classified cross-field links by count descending, then citing field ID and cited field ID ascending; show the top 25 for each, with displayed count and eligible count.

payload.text:
STATUS: done

Columbia-affiliated works made **39,134 citations to other works in the same 2021–2024 snapshot**. Among citations with both fields classified, **73.7% stayed within a field** and **26.3% crossed fields**. Medicine → Medicine was the largest flow (**6,765**). The largest cross-field flow was Medicine → Biochemistry, Genetics and Molecular Biology (**333**), closely followed by the reverse direction (**321**).

### Sankey: citing field → cited field

Default can be top 25 all to show dominance of same-field; provide a clear cross-field control. Use full labels in tooltip and sensible labels/no overlapping, readable chart. Separate left/right nodes for same field, and clear direction/ribbon width labels. If controls are not practical, supply two approved complementary views (all and cross-only).

Keep raw widths, label top-N cutoff and report total volume shown relative to mode denominator (all 39,134; cross 10,264). At top 25 these are 30,307 and 4,490 respectively. Flow direction is reference from citing to cited, not chronological knowledge direction.

STATUS: approved  
VIZ ARTIFACT: V1  
TITLE: Citation flows within Columbia research

**WHAT IT SHOWS:** The Sankey traces references from citing fields on the left to cited fields on the right for Columbia-to-Columbia citations in the 2021–2024 OpenAlex snapshot. Ribbon thickness encodes citation count, and teal distinguishes cross-field flows. **73.5% of all internal citations stay within the same field.** Medicine → Medicine is the largest flow (6,765 citations); Medicine → Biochemistry, Genetics and Molecular Biology is the largest cross-field flow (333).

Hover over a ribbon to see the full ordered field pair and count. Select a ribbon or field to emphasize that flow or its connected flows.

**PARAMETERS**
- **Flow mode** — Defaults to **All links eligible**. Switch to **Cross-field only** to show citations between different classified fields.
- **Top field-pair links** — Defaults to **25**, ranked by citation count. At that cutoff, all mode shows **30,307 of 39,134** eligible citations (77.4%); cross-field mode shows **4,490 of 10,264** (43.7%).

**VALIDATION:** The review gate approved the visualization. Headless checks passed for hover, selection, highlighting, and both parameter updates. Both default-cutoff views were visually checked.

**LIMITATIONS:** The chart shows only the ranked links within the cutoff, and widths rescale when filters change. Arrows follow references, not chronology. Unselected labels can become faint during selection. The automated mode-switch test checks that the view updates, but does not assert the exact cross-field coverage or validate every endpoint.

**About three quarters of Columbia-to-Columbia citations stayed within the same research field.** Of the 39,134 citations between works in the 2021–2024 Columbia snapshot, 28,778 stayed in the same field and 10,264 crossed fields—73.7% and 26.3%, respectively, among citations with both fields classified. | Biochemistry, Genetics and Molecular Biology → Medicine | 321 |
| Earth and Planetary Sciences → Environmental Science | 306 |
| Environmental Science → Earth and Planetary Sciences | 287 |

[T1, F1]

**Reading the Sankey:** The citing field is on the left, the cited field is on the right, and thicker ribbons mean more citations. Hover over a ribbon for its exact count. The diagram starts with the **25 largest flows**, covering **77.4%** of internal citations. Switch **Flow mode** to **Cross-field only** to see links that the large within-field flows can overshadow, or adjust **Top field-pair links** to show more or fewer ribbons. [V1, F1]

Each citation is counted once per directed work pair, and each work is assigned one field using its OpenAlex primary topic. Both works must be in the Columbia-affiliated snapshot, so references to older Columbia works are excluded. These are raw counts, not rates adjusted for field size. [T1, F1]

Two useful follow-ups: Which fields cite outside their own field most often *as a share* of their internal references? Which field pairs exchange more citations than their sizes would predict?
